draft.opening: After moving through {{priorSign}} from {{priorSignEntryDate}} to {{priorSignExitDate}}, Venus enters Libra on {{entryDate}}, and we pay closer attention to whether interest, effort, and consideration are being returned. Venus governs relationships, creativity, attraction, and what we value. Libra notices balance, exchange, connection, and how a shared choice is made. Because Venus rules Libra, finding common ground can feel unusually natural. That ease can make an agreement look fair and complete before both preferences are known.
draft.tension: The cost appears when agreement matters more than an honest answer. We ask what works for everyone else before admitting what works for us. Skill at compromise becomes automatic adjustment: we change a preference before anyone asks us to and treat the lack of disagreement as proof that the result is fair. The decision then belongs to whoever was clearest, while the more accommodating side carries the extra cost. Resentment enters an arrangement that still looks perfectly calm.
draft.development: In one collaboration, one person names a preference first. The other says it works and leaves their own preference unsaid. When that decision creates follow-up work or an added cost, the accommodating person takes it on rather than reopening what already looked settled. Each compromise seems small. Together they create a pattern in which the same person’s preferences keep moving and the same person keeps absorbing the consequences. The strategic shift is to state the preference before smoothing the arrangement. Once the withheld preference is stated, the other person’s response provides the real test: can the collaboration remain cooperative after both people say what they actually want? That response shows whether the connection can hold honesty, not just agreement.
draft.close: Before {{exitDate}}, an arrangement may strain when the person who kept agreeing can no longer accept what they do not want.

corrections.before: Until {{exitDate}}, the hierarchy gets harder to accept without question. The person doing the boss's job asks for that pay. Someone turns down the promotion that was really just more work in a nicer chair.
corrections.after: Until {{exitDate}}, the rules get harder to accept without question. The reliable person stops covering for someone else's lack of planning. Someone asks why the same standard changes depending on who broke it. A promotion gets turned down because it comes with more responsibility and no more authority.
corrections.owner_reason: Capricorn had collapsed into boss/title/career, functioning as the 10th house; broadened to responsibility, standards, legitimacy.
